bands.1:
Seven badges! Only one Keeper is left.

Kaydence Kray makes perfect pancakes for the whole crew.

Mo folds his arms. "They are suspicious pancakes."

The crew keeps all its proof in an old biscuit tin. The tin says, "NOT BISCUITS." It lives in the fridge, behind Mo's leftovers. Nobody ever touches Mo's leftovers.

Kaydence films Wren putting the tin away.

The next morning, the fridge is open. The tin is gone. So is Kaydence's purple speedboat, the Clickbait.

"Someone stole from MY fridge?" says Mo. "Nobody even steals my food!"

The tablet buzzes. Maxx is live. Kaydence is next to him, holding the tin.

"Vantafam!" says Maxx. "My new best friend Kaydence saved me from some lying pirates!"

He tips the tin into a gold shredder. Every piece of proof is chopped into confetti.

"That's Maxx-imum content!" he cries. "Kaydence will co-host my big live finale!"

Kaydence leans close to the camera. "Captain, remember that photo of your boat? I sent it to him. Stay cray!"

The screen goes black.

"Our proof is gone," says Tully. "Our chances are now zero."

Everyone looks at you.

Then BOLT-9 beeps. "Captain, I dusted every item in that tin. And I scan everything I dust."

His eyes shine onto the sail. Every piece of proof appears, perfectly copied.

"She took the tin," says BOLT-9. "She did not take the butler. I rate her plan four out of ten."

The crew cheers.

"Why was the tin so sad?" asks Mo. "It felt crumby!"

"It's NOT BISCUITS, Mo," says Zed.

"That's why it's sad."

The tablet buzzes again. Behind Maxx, a gold net the size of a footy field is lifted onto the yacht. Under the water, something huge glows.

"Biggest Rescue EVER, Live!" says Maxx. "Coming soon. Stay gold!"

You look at BOLT-9.

"I still have a key to his yacht, Captain," he says.

bands.4:
Seven badges! Only one Keeper is left to beat, and the crew can almost taste victory.

What they can actually taste is pancakes. To celebrate, Kaydence Kray cooks breakfast for the whole crew. Her pancakes are fluffy and golden, with crispy edges and a little pool of melting butter on top of each one. They are, annoyingly, perfect.

"Statistically, these are the best pancakes in the entire archipelago," says Tully, with her mouth full.

Mo folds his arms and glares at his own pan. "Statistically, they're suspicious."

The crew keeps all its proof in an old biscuit tin labelled "NOT BISCUITS". It lives in the fridge, hidden behind Mo's leftovers, because nobody ever goes near Mo's leftovers. Not even Mo.

That night, Kaydence films Wren tucking the tin back behind a bowl of something grey that might once have been soup. "Just for my viewers," she says, smiling her bright, careful smile.

The next morning, the fridge door is hanging open. The tin is gone. So is Kaydence's purple speedboat, the Clickbait, and every one of her ring lights.

A note is stuck to the fridge with a magnet: "Thanks for the snacks! Stay cray! xx K."

"Someone stole from MY fridge?" says Mo, genuinely shocked. "Nobody even steals my food!"

Then the tablet buzzes. Maxx is live on the sun deck of the Vantadome, and standing beside him, hugging the tin, is Kaydence.

"Vantafam, huge news!" says Maxx. "My new bestie Kaydence Kray has bravely rescued me from a gang of pirates who've been spreading LIES about me! Smash that heart button for Kaydence!"

He tips the tin into a gold shredder. Every piece of proof the crew has risked everything for is chopped into glittering confetti, which Maxx throws over his own head.

"That's Maxx-imum content!" he cries. "And to say thank you, Kaydence will co-host my live finale. That's seventy-nine million followers, together at last!"

Kaydence leans close to the camera, and her smile goes thin. "Oh, and Captain? Remember that photo of your leaky little boat that Maxx showed everyone, right at the very start? Who do you think sent it to him? Stay cray!"

The screen goes black.

For a long moment, the only sound is the drip of the leak. Indi draws a moustache on Kaydence in her sketchbook, then a second moustache on top of the first, then a monobrow.

"Classic betrayal arc," says Zed miserably. "She never once switched her camera off. I should have seen that boss fight coming."

"Without proof," says Tully, "our chances are now zero per cent. I checked twice."

Wren just stares at the empty shelf in the fridge. Slowly, everyone turns to look at you.

Then BOLT-9 gives a small, polite beep. "Captain, may I? I dusted every item in that tin, because it was filthy. And I scan everything I dust."

His eyes beam onto the sail like a projector. One by one, every piece of proof appears, copied perfectly, right down to the fingerprints and the gold pen.

"Miss Kray took the tin," says BOLT-9. "She did not take the butler. I rate her plan four out of ten."

The crew cheers so loudly that the Soggy Biscuit springs a fresh leak. Gus hugs the robot, and BOLT-9 dusts him, which Gus seems to enjoy.

"Why was the biscuit tin so sad?" asks Mo, cheering up at once. "It was feeling crumby!"

"It's NOT BISCUITS, Mo," says Zed.

"That's exactly why it's sad."

Then the tablet buzzes again. Maxx is still live, and still gloating. Behind him, a crane is lifting a gold net the size of a footy field onto the deck of the Vantadome. Deep in the dark water below the yacht, something enormous begins, very slowly, to glow.

"Biggest Rescue EVER, Live!" says Maxx, flashing his blinding teeth. "Coming soon, Vantafam. Stay gold!"

You look at BOLT-9.

"I still have a key to the Vantadome, Captain," he says. "I rate this plan ten out of ten."
